# Course Schedule {.unnumbered}

The full day-by-day plan for the redesigned course. This mirrors
`course-redesign.md` in the repository root, which has the full rationale,
licensing notes, and open questions behind this structure. Days already
written link to their page; the rest are still to come — the pattern is
established on Days 1, 2, 4, and 6 and the remaining days will follow it.

Three phases: bioinformatics foundations build up to profiles (Days 3-5);
a convergence zone (Days 6-9) where the classical material directly
motivates and is resolved by neural networks; then a deep-learning arc
(Days 10-12) that keeps extending the same secondary-structure-prediction
thread.

| # | Session | Primary reading (open, linked) | Biological case study | Lab |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [**Math prerequisites**](day01.qmd) — linear algebra, calculus, probability refresher | d2l.ai, [Preliminaries](https://d2l.ai/chapter_preliminaries/index.html) (§2.3 Linear Algebra, §2.5 Calculus, §2.6 Probability & Statistics) | — | None (non-code problem set) |
| 2 | [**Programming prerequisites**](day02.qmd) — Python incl. classes/OOP, then array programming | [*A Byte of Python*](https://python.swaroopch.com/) (ch. "Object Oriented Programming" for classes); d2l.ai [Preliminaries](https://d2l.ai/chapter_preliminaries/index.html) §2.1 Data Manipulation, §2.2 Preprocessing, §2.5 Automatic Differentiation | — | **Full** |
| 3 | [**Biological Databases**](day03.qmd) | Wikipedia: [Biological database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_database), [Sequence database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequence_database); NCBI: [GenBank overview](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genbank/); practice via EMBL-EBI Training's [What is ENA?](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/ena-quick-tour/what-is-ena/) and [The UniProt databases](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/uniprot-quick-tour/the-uniprot-databases/) | The *HBB* (beta-globin) locus | Light exercise |
| 4 | [**Sequence Alignment**](day04.qmd) | Wikipedia: [Needleman–Wunsch algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Needleman%E2%80%93Wunsch_algorithm), [Smith–Waterman algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smith%E2%80%93Waterman_algorithm), [Substitution matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitution_matrix) (BLOSUM/PAM); practice: EMBL-EBI [Pairwise Sequence Alignment](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/guide-to-sequence-analysis-tools/sequence-alignment/pairwise-sequence-alignment/) and [Multiple Sequence Alignment](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/guide-to-sequence-analysis-tools/sequence-alignment/multiple-sequence-alignment/) | Aligning two homologous globins | Light exercise |
| 5 | [**Advanced Database Search & Profile Methods (BLAST, PSSMs, HMMs)**](day05.qmd) *(merged)* | Wikipedia: [BLAST (biotechnology)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BLAST_(biotechnology)), [Hidden Markov model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hidden_Markov_model), [Position weight matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Position_weight_matrix), [Sequence profiling tool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequence_profiling_tool); NCBI: [BLAST® Help](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1762/) (public domain) | A real BLAST search on an unknown sequence, followed by PSI-BLAST/a Pfam domain search on the same family — framed explicitly as: a profile/PSSM score is a weighted sum over positions, i.e. already a linear model | **Full** (covers Day 4+5 alignment practice, BLAST, and profile/HMM search together) |
| 6 | [**Linear models, gradient descent & the XOR problem**](day06.qmd) | d2l.ai, [Linear Neural Networks for Regression](https://d2l.ai/chapter_linear-regression/index.html); Wikipedia [Perceptron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perceptron), [*Perceptrons* (book)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perceptrons_(book)); [Bulyk, Johnson & Church (2002)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11861919/), *Nucleic Acids Research* 30(5):1255-1261 | Formalize Day 5's profile score as a perceptron; show its weights can be *learned* by gradient descent instead of derived from alignment statistics; then the real-world punchline — non-additive positional dependence in a transcription factor binding site, the same limitation the classic XOR problem illustrates | **Full** |
| 7 | [**Protein Structure**](day07.qmd) | Wikipedia: [Protein structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_structure); [RCSB PDB-101](https://pdb101.rcsb.org/) | Hemoglobin structure in PyMOL, plus a descriptive preview of Rost & Sander's early-1990s PHD method | **Full** (PyMOL) |
| 8 | [**Linear classification (softmax) + practical PyTorch**](day08.qmd) | d2l.ai, [Linear Neural Networks for Classification](https://d2l.ai/chapter_linear-classification/index.html) + [Builders' Guide](https://d2l.ai/chapter_builders-guide/index.html) | **Subcellular localization** prediction; the vehicle for teaching real PyTorch idioms (writing a model as a class, closing the loop with Day 2's OOP) | **Full** |
| 9 | [**Multilayer Perceptrons**](day09.qmd) — nonlinearity, backprop, initialization, generalization, dropout | d2l.ai, [Multilayer Perceptrons](https://d2l.ai/chapter_multilayer-perceptrons/index.html) | **Payoff of Days 5-8**: Rost & Sander's PHD method end-to-end — profile input → hidden layer → 3-class softmax output → secondary structure | **Full** |
| 10 | [**CNNs**](day10.qmd), classic & modern | d2l.ai, [Convolutional Neural Networks](https://d2l.ai/chapter_convolutional-neural-networks/index.html) + [Modern Convolutional Neural Networks](https://d2l.ai/chapter_convolutional-modern/index.html) | Protein contact prediction; SS-prediction's later profile+CNN era | **Full** |
| 11 | [**RNNs & LSTM**](day11.qmd) | d2l.ai, [Recurrent Neural Networks](https://d2l.ai/chapter_recurrent-neural-networks/index.html) + [Modern Recurrent Neural Networks](https://d2l.ai/chapter_recurrent-modern/index.html) | SignalP signal-peptide detection; SS-prediction's (bi)LSTM era | Light exercise |
| 12 | [**Attention & Transformers**](day12.qmd) | d2l.ai, [Attention Mechanisms and Transformers](https://d2l.ai/chapter_attention-mechanisms-and-transformers/index.html) | **AlphaFold** + **protein language models** — SS-prediction's endpoint | Light exercise |
| — | [**Capstone: Secondary Structure Prediction project**](capstone.qmd) | — | Closes the loop opened at Day 7 | The project itself |
